info.description:
Better Metadata - Better Science

Folders and artifacts use type-qualified selectors: `folders/<uuid>`, `templates/<uuid>`,
`template-elements/<uuid>`, `template-fields/<uuid>`, or `template-instances/<uuid>`.
Typed routes include the type once, for example `/templates/<uuid>`. Query parameters and
command-body selectors retain the type, including folder parameters. Percent-encoded full
IRIs remain accepted for compatibility. Stored document identities and references remain
full IRIs; legacy repository hosts must remain absolute until their data is migrated.

The bridge server is CEDAR's connection to registries outside it. It mints DOIs through DataCite
so a CEDAR artifact can be cited, and it resolves and searches identifiers held by seven external
authorities: DOI, NIH grants, ORCID, CompTox, PubMed, ROR and RRID.

An upstream refusal is answered in the shared error body with the key `upstreamServerError`,
rather than flattened into a 500. Its parameters name the upstream service and the status it
answered, and its objects carry what it answered. A refusal keeps the upstream status, except that
DataCite or an external registry failing, refusing this deployment's credentials or access, or
limiting its requests answers 502, as does an upstream answer that is neither a success nor a
refusal. The external-authority routes, which take no credentials, therefore never answer 401.

get.description: Return everything the workbench needs to open the DOI form for one artifact: the DataCite metadata template, the source artifact, and either the draft DOI already started for it or a metadata instance pre-filled with what can be derived. Reads only; nothing is minted here. DataCite integration can be switched off by configuration, and every route here answers 400 when it is.

post.description: Register a DOI with DataCite from the metadata instance in the body, and record it on the artifact. `state` chooses between a draft, which can still be changed, and a published DOI, which is findable and permanent. The metadata is validated against the DataCite template first, and a failure is returned rather than half-registered. DataCite integration can be switched off by configuration, and every route here answers 400 when it is.

The resource server refusing a read is also reported (upstreamServerError).

get.summary: Get a DOI's metadata from DataCite

get.description: These routes take no credentials. Neither builds a request context, so anyone who can reach this host can use them, and three of the seven authorities behind them spend credentials the deployment holds. Recorded here because a spec that claimed otherwise would be worse than one that says so. Search one external authority for entries matching a name, and return them with the paging that produced them. A registry's refusal is answered in the shared error body (upstreamServerError), with the registry's status in parameters.upstreamStatusCode, the registry in parameters.upstreamService, and the authority's answer in objects.authorityAnswer, where `found` is false. A refusal of the request itself keeps the registry's status, which may be one not listed below, such as 409. A registry that refuses this deployment's access (401 or 403), limits its requests (429) or fails (5xx) is a 502, since the caller can do nothing about it. So is a status that is neither 200 nor an error, such as a redirect. These routes therefore never answer 401. A registry that does not answer is a 503, and one whose answer cannot be read is a 502. An authority that has not finished loading answers 503 with Retry-After rather than an empty result.

parameters.description: Which registry to ask. One of `doi`, `nih-grant`, `orcid`, `comp-tox`, `pmid`, `ror`, `rrid`. A segment no authority is registered under answers 404 naming the ones that are.
parameters.name: authority

parameters.description: How many entries to return, from 1 to 500. Defaults to 100.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: How many matching entries to skip. Defaults to 0.
parameters.name: offset

parameters.description: Zero-based page number, for clients that page by number. Cannot be sent with `limit` or `offset`. Defaults to 0.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: Entries per page, for clients that page by number. Cannot be sent with `limit` or `offset`. Defaults to 100, and must be greater than one and at most 500.
parameters.name: pageSize

200.description: A page of matching entries, with the paging envelope and, for clients that still page by number, `found`, `page` and `pageSize`

400.description: The limit or offset is out of range, `page` is negative or `pageSize` is not greater than one, both kinds of paging were sent, or a paging parameter is not a number. The registry refusing the search with 400 is reported too (upstreamServerError).

404.description: No authority is served under this path segment (no error key, and the message names the segments that are served), or the registry answered the search with 404 (upstreamServerError)

406.description: The request does not accept a JSON response

502.description: The registry answered with something that could not be read, or ORCID refused the credentials this server holds. A registry that refuses this deployment's access (401 or 403), limits its requests (429), fails (5xx), or answers with a status that is neither 200 nor an error is reported as upstreamServerError, with its status in parameters.upstreamStatusCode.

503.description: The registry did not answer, or the authority is not ready yet, in which case Retry-After says when to try again.

get.summary: Search an external registry by name

post.description: Recognizes the authority-specific IRI, then resolves its exact identifier using the configured authority and circuit breaker. Returns a passed, failed or unavailable semantic fact, independently of save policy. No arbitrary submitted URL is fetched. DataCite absence is unavailable because DataCite does not register every DOI.

404.description: No authority is served under this path segment (no error key, and the message names the segments that are served)

get.description: These routes take no credentials. Neither builds a request context, so anyone who can reach this host can use them, and three of the seven authorities behind them spend credentials the deployment holds. Recorded here because a spec that claimed otherwise would be worse than one that says so. Look one identifier up in an external authority and return what it holds, with `found` saying whether it resolved and `requestedId` echoing what was asked. A registry's refusal is answered in the shared error body (upstreamServerError), with the registry's status in parameters.upstreamStatusCode, the registry in parameters.upstreamService, and the authority's answer in objects.authorityAnswer, where `found` is false and `requestedId` echoes what was asked. A refusal of the request itself keeps the registry's status, which may be one not listed below, such as 409. A registry that refuses this deployment's access (401 or 403), limits its requests (429) or fails (5xx) is a 502, since the caller can do nothing about it. So is a status that is neither 200 nor an error, such as a redirect. These routes therefore never answer 401. A failed lookup is a 502, so it is never reported as an identifier the registry does not hold. A registry that does not answer is a 503, and one whose answer cannot be read is a 502. This path and the search path both match two segments; the literal `search-by-name` wins, so no authority can have an entry by that name.

parameters.description: Which registry to ask. One of `doi`, `nih-grant`, `orcid`, `comp-tox`, `pmid`, `ror`, `rrid`. A segment no authority is registered under answers 404 naming the ones that are.
parameters.name: authority

parameters.description: The identifier to resolve, as that registry spells it.
parameters.name: id

200.description: What the authority holds for the identifier

400.description: The registry refused the lookup with 400 (upstreamServerError)

404.description: No authority is served under this path segment (no error key, and the message names the segments that are served), or ORCID or ROR holds no entry for the identifier (upstreamServerError). The body's objects.authorityAnswer then holds the authority's answer, with `found` false, `requestedId`, and the registry's own answer under `rawResponse`. The other authorities answer 200 with `found` false for an identifier their registry does not hold.

406.description: The request does not accept a JSON response

502.description: The registry answered with something that could not be read, or ORCID refused the credentials this server holds. A registry that refuses this deployment's access (401 or 403), limits its requests (429), fails (5xx), or answers with a status that is neither 200 nor an error is reported as upstreamServerError, with its status in parameters.upstreamStatusCode.

503.description: The registry did not answer, or the authority is not ready yet, in which case Retry-After says when to try again.

AuthorityDetails.description:
What one authority holds for one identifier. Only `found` and `requestedId` are added by
CEDAR; the rest of the object is the authority's own, and the keys below are the ones every
authority sets when it resolves an identifier. ORCID and ROR also pass the registry's whole
record through under `rawResponse`. A registry's refusal is answered in the shared error body,
whose `objects.authorityAnswer` holds this object with `found` false. There ORCID and ROR
carry the registry's own answer under `rawResponse`, null when it was not JSON, and its reasons
under `errors`.

details.description: A line of supporting detail, where the authority composes one.

errors.description:
What the registry said went wrong, one message per entry. Set by ORCID and ROR, and only
in a refusal's `objects.authorityAnswer`.

id.description: The entry's IRI, as the authority spells it.

name.description: The entry's display name. Null where the identifier did not resolve.

rawResponse.description: The registry's own record, unchanged, where the authority passes it through.

requestedId.description: The identifier as it was asked for.

AuthoritySearchRequest.description: The page that was asked for, after defaults were applied.

AuthoritySearchResults.description:
The entries one authority offers for a name, in CEDAR's paging envelope. A registry's refusal
is not a page. It is answered in the shared error body, with `found`, `results` and any reasons
the authority read off the refusal in `objects.authorityAnswer`. `found`, `page` and `pageSize`
are the fields the route answered with before it took `limit` and `offset`, kept for clients
that still page by number.

countCapped.description: Present and true when `totalCount` is a lower bound. There is then no `last` link.

currentOffset.description: The offset of the first entry on this page.

found.description: Whether the registry answered and offered at least one entry.

page.description: The zero-based page returned, defaulted to 0.

pageSize.description: The page size used, defaulted to 100.

paging.description: Links to the first, previous, next and last pages, keyed by relation. A relation with no page is absent.

results.description: One entry per matching term, keyed by the term's IRI, in the order the registry offered them.

totalCount.description:
How many entries match. A lower bound when `countCapped` is true: ROR can be read only
one upstream page deep, and NIH RePORTER narrows its answers after the fact and cannot
know its total at all.

AuthorityTerm.description: One entry an authority offers for a name.

details.description:
A line of supporting detail the authority composes to tell one entry from another of the
same name. Its wording is the authority's own.

name.description: The entry's display name, chosen by the authority from the names the registry holds.

CedarError.description: A CEDAR error response. Diagnostic fields are populated only when they are relevant to the failure.

additionalProperties.description: Named domain entities associated with exception-mapped errors.

entities.description: Named domain entities associated with exception-mapped errors.

errorId.description: Correlation identifier for an internal error recorded in server logs.

errorReasonKey.description: More specific machine-readable reason for the error.

additionalProperties.description: Named structured values associated with the error.

objects.description: Named structured values associated with the error.

operation.description: Operation that failed. Its fields depend on the operation type.

additionalProperties.description: Named scalar values associated with the error.

parameters.description: Named scalar values associated with the error.

status.description: Symbolic HTTP response status, or HTTP_<code> for an unnamed status.

suggestedAction.description: Recovery action suggested to the client.

DataCiteDoiMetadata.description:
What DataCite holds for the DOI, as DataCite returned it: its JSON:API document, requested
with affiliation detail. The keys below are the ones that document always carries; everything
under `attributes` is DataCite's own and follows the DataCite metadata schema.

attributes.description: The DOI's metadata, as DataCite models it.

DoiFormStart.description:
Everything the workbench needs to open the DOI form for one artifact: the DataCite metadata
template, the source artifact, and either the draft DOI already started for it or a metadata
instance pre-filled with what could be derived.

dataCiteTemplate.description:
The DataCite metadata template the form is rendered from, as the artifact server returned
it. An open CEDAR JSON-LD template, its identifier fixed by configuration.

draftDoi.description: The draft DOI DataCite already holds for the artifact, or null where it holds none.

existingDataCiteMetadata.description:
The metadata the form opens with, as an instance of the DataCite metadata template.
Converted from the draft DOI where DataCite already holds one for the artifact, and
otherwise pre-filled with the artifact's URL and resource type alone.

sourceArtifact.description:
The source artifact, as the artifact server returned it. An open CEDAR JSON-LD artifact
of the kind `sourceArtifactType` names.

sourceArtifactType.description: The kind of artifact the DOI is for.

DoiRegistration.description: The DOI as DataCite registered it.

dataCiteResponse.description: DataCite's own response body, passed through as the string it arrived as rather than reparsed.

doiId.description: The DOI without a resolver prefix, as DataCite identifies it.

doiName.description: The same DOI as a resolvable URL.

InstanceArtifactDocument.description: A template instance. Its value keys are the names of the template's fields and elements, so the only fixed key beyond the common artifact keys is the template it is based on.

@context.description: JSON-LD context for the keys the artifact uses.

@id.description: The artifact's IRI. The server mints it on a POST, so a body sent to POST carries none; a body sent to PUT carries the IRI of the path.

oslc:modifiedBy.description: IRI of the user who last changed it.

pav:createdBy.description: IRI of the user who created it.

pav:lastUpdatedOn.description: When the artifact was last changed.

schema:isBasedOn.description: IRI of the template the instance was filled in against.

api_key.description: Your CEDAR API key, using the format 'apiKey <yourApiKey>'
api_key.name: Authorization
